Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the detailed discussion on your integration patterns and security requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

1) What we heard (recap)
- Primary integration: server-to-server API calls from FintechCo backend to Redwood-hosted endpoints for structured output + embeddings/rerank.
- Key concerns: strong key management, automated rotation, short-lived tokens for principals, and integration with your KMS (HashiCorp Vault).
- Desired outcome: minimal ops work on your side for rotation and auditing, plus support for service accounts and OAuth/JWT option for token issuance.

2) Recommended short-term approach (MVP)
- Use service accounts with short-lived JWT/OAuth tokens (client credentials flow) for production; fallback API keys for non-critical integrations (dev/CI).
- Redwood provides a key rotation API and Audit logs (we'll share scope in the implementation guide).
- Integrations: SDKs support automatic token refresh; embedding/rerank calls can use the same tokens.

3) Action items / owners

- Redwood (Rishi): share a short sample JWT exchange and a recommended rotation cadence for service accounts / API keys.

Hi Alex / Priya — looping in a few quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive. Short answers first, then an attachable example (jwt-sample.txt) you can try locally.

1) JWT / service account flow (recommended for Prod) - You create a service account in Redwood Console and either: (A) upload a public key (if you want to sign JWTs client-side) or (B) provide Redwood with a service credential that we exchange for tokens.
- If you sign JWTs client-side: FintechCo signs a short-lived JWT (claims: iss=fintechco-sa, sub=integration, aud=https://api.redwood.com/token), Redwood validates signature against the uploaded public key, then issues an access token (short TTL, e.g., 15m) bound to the integration.
- If you prefer OAuth2 client_credentials: Redwood can accept tokens issued by your auth server; we validate via JWKS or introspection. This is a good option if you already have an internal token service.

2) Token rotation / TTLs
- Service-account access tokens: short TTL (10-30m) + automatic refresh via SDK (recommended).
- Long-lived service credentials (private keys): rotate on a schedule (90 days recommended) and revoke via the Redwood Console or API.
- API keys: treat as long-lived but rotate quarterly; Redwood supports key versioning and a rollover endpoint to swap keys with zero downtime.

3) Implementation notes & audit
- Redwood provides an Audit Logs API that surfaces key creation, rotation, and token issuance events.
- SDKs: automatic refresh + transparent retry of in-flight requests during key rollover.

Example (very small, see attached jwt-sample.txt for full):

# sign_and_exchange.sh (conceptual)
# 1) Sign a JWT with FintechCo service account private key
# 2) POST to https://api.redwood.com/token to exchange for access token

cat <<EOF > request.jwt
{
  "iss": "fintechco-sa",
  "sub": "integration-service",
  "aud": "https://api.redwood.com/token",
  "exp": $(($(date +%s) + 300))
}
EOF

# sign with your private key, then curl to Redwood token endpoint
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/token -d @signed.jwt -H 'Content-Type: application/jwt'

Happy to walk through live examples on the call — we'll also bring a short demo using the Python SDK showing auto-refresh.
